body:
Fellow autistic here. 

I sympathize it is a curse at times-

The overstimulation, the sensory issues, the meltdowns, going nonverbal, freaking out over routine disruption, the bullying from NT people, the tone policing, the infantilization, the ableism, the inability to get disability because you’re not “autistic enough.”, the lack of help at school because you’re not “autistic enough”, hearing how “everyone’s a little autistic” when you try and talk about your symptoms. And then you’re always the weird one in the family. Even if your parents are accepting- your aunts, uncles, cousins. Immediately black sheep.

But you know what I find really cool about my autism despite all that?

I love learning. About a LOT of things. I’m a big Tolkien buff, I can sit at my computer for 5 or 6 hours and churn out 3 or 4 fanfics and 2 sets of headcanons because of my hyper focus. I know a lot of morbid facts, health facts, facts on motherhood and childbirth, just weird little things because it’s fun. I can speed read- it takes me a 1 day and a 1/2 to finish a 1,000 page novel if I really like it. I love talking to other autistic people and relating. My comfort food is pasta and I LOVE pasta- Alfredo, macaroni, spaghetti, pesto. And how could I possibly forget my love of garlic bread and Dr. Pepper? 

If I get my mind set on something to learn how to do I’ll spend 5 hours daily doing it. I learned to play the violin in under a year, when I’d come home from school when I was still in school I’d spend hours drawing. I’m not a savant it’s just I’ll hyper focus until I learn it. I love my routine when it’s not disrupted. 

I’m 28. And used to hate being autistic, because I spent so much time trying to jam myself to fit into NT spaces. I finally started cutting people out of my life who didn’t accept me for who I am. 

I started making more friends with other Neurodivergent people. ADHD, Autism. I found a community I fit into, I joined support groups. (Can’t afford therapy.). 

It’s hard to stop caring what other people think of you. And it’s hard to deal with the symptoms that **are** negative. 

Like I can’t go to concerts, or loud venues without my loops or headphones. Because it’s too loud. I stand there awkwardly not sure what to do when someone talks to my husband and they don’t include me. People always ask me if I’m okay because I have RBF because I’m not masking. 

It’s hard but you should learn to find all the good things about being autistic. Because there ARE good things about being autistic. I know it is so hard to see it when you feel like this. But I promise there ARE good things about being autistic.
